title: Bright white, and delicious to drink.
subtitle: Pleasure with nothing ugly in it

row.title: delicious
sub: taste as good as its look

then: Zayd bin Aslam said it is {reward}white flowing{/reward}, a bright shining colour, unlike this world's drinks that a sound nature finds repulsive. Ibn Kathir says {reward}its taste will be as good as its colour.{/reward}
now: The energy drink tastes great and leaves you shaky. The late-night snack feels good and you regret it at 2am. {trap}So many pleasures here come with a bill.{/trap} {reward}This one does not.{/reward}
old: Every pleasure has a downside I have to accept.
new: Allah has pleasure waiting that has no downside at all.
try: Skip one pleasure today that you know leaves you feeling worse afterwards.

title: No headache, no losing your mind.
subtitle: Joy that keeps you clear
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said ghawl means {trap}stomach aches and such effects{/trap}. Mujahid said it {reward}will not cause them to lose their minds.{/reward} Ibn Abbas listed four harms of this world's wine; Paradise's drink is free of all of them.
now: You come home exhausted and want to switch off: hours of scrolling, numbing out. You wake up foggier. {reward}The joy of Paradise does not take you away from yourself.{/reward} It makes you more awake.
old: Real relaxation means switching my mind off.
new: The best joy keeps me clear and present, not numb.
try: Replace twenty minutes of numbing out tonight with something that leaves you clear: a walk, a call, some Quran.

title: Companions whose eyes are for them alone.
subtitle: Loyalty as part of the reward
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others said these are {reward}chaste companions who will not look at anyone other than their husbands.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says their eyes are described as {reward}beautiful and chaste{/reward} together.
now: Your phone is full of images built to pull your eyes away from the person beside you. {idea}Here, the picture of beauty is a gaze that stays faithful.{/idea} Guarding your own gaze is part of that beauty now.
old: Where my eyes wander does not hurt anyone.
new: A faithful gaze is part of what Allah calls beautiful, and I can practise it now.
try: Lower your gaze once today when you notice it wandering, and say astaghfirullah.

title: Like well-protected, untouched pearls.
subtitle: Something precious kept safe
then: Ibn Abbas said it means {reward}as if they were hidden pearls{/reward}. Al-Hasan said protected, {reward}never touched by any hands.{/reward} Others said the inside of an egg, beneath the shell, which no hand reaches.
now: You keep your most precious things somewhere safe: the ring in a box, documents in a drawer, not left on the bus seat. {reward}What is precious is protected.{/reward} That applies to your heart and your dignity too.
old: Something is only valuable if everyone can see it.
new: The most precious things are guarded, and that care is part of their worth.
try: Keep one private thing private today that you might have posted or shared.

title: In Paradise, friends turn to each other and talk.
subtitle: Remembering the road that got them there

row.title: their stories
sub: how life was, what they suffered

then: Ibn Kathir says the people of Paradise will ask one another {reward}how they were in this world and what they suffered{/reward}, while they sit together and servants bring them delights no eye has seen.
now: You are in the middle of a hard year: the job loss, the illness, the long nights. {reward}One day it may be a story you tell, smiling, among friends in the gardens.{/reward} Today is a chapter, not the ending.
old: What I am going through now is just pointless pain.
new: The hard parts of my life can become stories of how Allah carried me.
try: Tell one friend today about a hard time Allah helped you through.

title: I had a companion back in the world.
subtitle: A memory of a friend who doubted
then: Ibn Abbas said this refers to {idea}an idolator man who had a believing companion{/idea} in this world. Ibn Kathir also mentions a report of two business partners: one spent on himself, the other gave in charity.
now: You think of your oldest friends: the one from school, the colleague you lunch with every day. {idea}Each of them is quietly pulling you in a direction.{/idea} One day you will remember which way.
old: My friendships do not affect my faith.
new: My companions shape my path, so I choose and influence them with care.
try: Think of one friend you love who doubts. Make a sincere dua for them by name.

title: He kept asking: you really believe all this?
subtitle: The quiet pressure of a doubting friend
then: Ibn Kathir says he asked whether his friend believed in {idea}the resurrection, the Reckoning, and reward{/idea}, and said it {trap}by way of astonishment, disbelief and stubbornness.{/trap}
now: Lunch at work. Someone says, wait, you actually believe in all that? Everyone looks at you. {trap}The question is light; the pressure is heavy.{/trap} The believer in this story held on.
old: If smart people around me find it strange, maybe it is.
new: A friend's surprise is not an argument; I can stay firm and kind.
try: If someone questions your faith today, answer calmly with one sentence you truly believe.

title: Once we are dust, we will be held to account?
subtitle: The doubt that deeds really count
then: Mujahid and As-Suddi said madinun means {idea}brought to account.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said {idea}rewarded or punished according to our deeds.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says both views are correct.
now: You cheat a little on expenses and think: who will ever know, it is tiny. You help a stranger and think: it does not really matter. {idea}Both get counted.{/idea}
old: Small things do not really count in the end.
new: Every deed, small or big, is brought to account.
try: Do one small honest thing today that no one would notice if you skipped it.

title: Would you like to look?
subtitle: A believer wonders where his friend ended up
then: Ibn Kathir says the believer {idea}says this to his companions among the people of Paradise{/idea}: will you look over? He remembers his old friend and wants to know where he is.
now: You scroll through old contacts and wonder what happened to people you once spent every day with. {idea}Close friends can end up in very different places.{/idea} The path you walk together matters.
old: We will always be close, whatever we each believe.
new: Friends can end up far apart, so I want to walk with mine toward Allah.
try: Invite one friend to something good this week: a class, a prayer, a charity visit.

title: He looked, and saw him in the middle of the Fire.
subtitle: The friend's choice reached its end
then: Ibn Abbas and others said it means {trap}in the middle of Hell.{/trap} The two had been companions in the world. Their paths split over one question: {idea}do you believe in the meeting with Allah?{/idea}
now: Two kids sit at the same school desk. Same teacher, same chances. Twenty years later, one built a good life, one lost his way. {idea}Small choices, repeated, decide the end.{/idea} Yours are still being made.
old: We are friends, so we will end up the same way.
new: My own choices decide my end, whoever I sit beside.
try: Make one choice today you would be glad to look back on.

title: By Allah, you almost ruined me.
subtitle: How close the danger really was
then: Ibn Kathir says the believer tells the disbeliever: {trap}by Allah, you nearly caused me to be doomed, if I had obeyed you.{/trap} Only now does he see how close the danger was.
now: The friend who said, come on, just this once. The group that almost pulled you in. Looking back, you shiver at how close it was. {trap}Some influences nearly cost us everything.{/trap}
old: I would never have fallen for that.
new: I was closer to the edge than I knew, and I need to watch who pulls on me.
try: Name one influence that almost pulled you away from Allah. Thank Him for saving you.

title: If not for my Lord's favour, I would be there too.
subtitle: Guidance as a gift, not an achievement
then: Ibn Kathir says the believer means: {reward}He bestowed His grace upon me, had mercy upon me and guided me to faith.{/reward} He links it to 7:43: we could never have found guidance had Allah not guided us.
now: You see someone struggling with addiction or anger and feel a little proud that you are not like them. {reward}Your steadiness is a gift.{/reward} Without His favour, it could be you.
old: I am on the right path because I made good choices.
new: I am guided because Allah was kind to me, so I stay humble and thankful.
try: When you see someone struggling today, say alhamdulillah quietly and make dua for them.

title: So we will never die again?
subtitle: The joy of a life with no ending
then: Ibn Kathir says the believers say this {reward}when they feel joy{/reward} at what Allah has given them, realising they will remain forever. Al-Hasan said: {trap}they know that death ends every delight{/trap}, so they ask.
now: Even on your happiest day, at a wedding, holding a newborn, a small voice says: this will not last. {trap}Every joy here has an edge.{/trap} {reward}In Paradise the edge is gone.{/reward}
old: Every happy moment is shadowed by knowing it will end.
new: There is a happiness coming that never has to end.
try: In a happy moment today, say: O Allah, give me the joy that never ends.

title: Only that first death, and no punishment.
subtitle: The worst is behind them forever
then: Ibn Kathir says the believers realise {reward}they are to remain in Paradise forever, with no punishment and no death to come.{/reward} The only death they will ever know is the one already behind them.
now: You lie awake some nights afraid of dying, of losing your parents, of the hospital corridor. {reward}For the believer, death is one door, walked through once.{/reward} After that, never again.
old: Death is the thing I fear most.
new: For the believer, death is one door, and what lies past it is safety.
try: When the fear of death comes today, say: O Allah, make my last day my best day.

title: This is the great success.
subtitle: What winning actually means
then: Al-Hasan said that when they ask whether they will die again, {reward}it will be said: no, truly this is the supreme success.{/reward} Ibn Kathir reads the next verse with it: {idea}for the like of this, let the workers work.{/idea}
now: Your LinkedIn says success is a new title. Your feed says it is a car or a holiday. You chase it every day. {reward}The verse names the real win{/reward}, and every small good deed is work toward it.
old: Success is what I can show people now.
new: The great success is Paradise, and I work for it in small ways every day.
try: Write down one goal for this week that works toward the great success, and start it today.
